import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source_files = {
    "Source6_71_0": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_0.csv",
    "Source6_71_1": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_1.csv",
    "Source6_71_2": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_2.csv",
    "Source6_71_3": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_3.csv",
    "Source6_71_4": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_4.csv",
    "Source6_71_5": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_5.csv",
    "Source6_71_6": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_6.csv",
    "Source6_71_7": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_7.csv",
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_71_0"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Albums in RS500']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_71_1"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Score']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_71_2"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_71_3"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Times on Cover of RS']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_71_4"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Spotify']
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_71_5"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_71_6"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Certified Units (Millions)']
df7 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_71_7"], index_col=0)  # ['Artist', 'Influenced']

# Step 2: Merge all source tables on 'Artist' using left joins progressively
# Start from df2 because it has multiple columns and is a good base (Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated)
df_merged = df2.copy()

# Merge df0: Albums in RS500
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df0[['Artist', 'Albums in RS500']], on='Artist', how='left')

# Merge df1: Score
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df1[['Artist', 'Score']], on='Artist', how='left')

# Merge df3: Times on Cover of RS
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df3[['Artist', 'Times on Cover of RS']], on='Artist', how='left')

# Merge df4: Spotify
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df4[['Artist', 'Spotify']], on='Artist', how='left')

# Merge df5: Top 100 Singles, Highest Position
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df5[['Artist', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position']], on='Artist', how='left')

# Merge df6: Certified Units (Millions)
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df6[['Artist', 'Certified Units (Millions)']], on='Artist', how='left')

# Merge df7: Influenced
df_merged = df_merged.merge(df7[['Artist', 'Influenced']], on='Artist', how='left')

# Step 3: Ensure all target columns exist in the final dataframe
# Target Schema:
# ['Artist': string, 'Year Inducted': float, 'Years Waited': integer, '# of Years Nominated': integer,
#  'Influenced': integer, 'Certified Units (Millions)': float, 'Albums in RS500': integer,
#  'Top 100 Singles': integer, 'Highest Position': integer, 'Times on Cover of RS': integer,
#  'Score': float, 'Spotify': integer]

# Step 4: Data type conversions and filling missing values if necessary
# Convert columns to appropriate types, allowing NaNs where float is expected

# 'Year Inducted' is float (NaNs allowed)
df_merged['Year Inducted'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Year Inducted'], errors='coerce')

# 'Years Waited' integer (NaNs allowed, convert to Int64 to allow nullable integers)
df_merged['Years Waited'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Years Waited'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# '# of Years Nominated' integer nullable
df_merged['# of Years Nominated'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['# of Years Nominated'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Influenced' integer nullable
df_merged['Influenced'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Influenced'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Certified Units (Millions)' float
df_merged['Certified Units (Millions)'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Certified Units (Millions)'], errors='coerce')

# 'Albums in RS500' integer nullable
df_merged['Albums in RS500'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Albums in RS500'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Top 100 Singles' integer nullable
df_merged['Top 100 Singles'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Top 100 Singles'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Highest Position' integer nullable
df_merged['Highest Position'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Highest Position'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Times on Cover of RS' integer nullable
df_merged['Times on Cover of RS'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Times on Cover of RS'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# 'Score' float
df_merged['Score'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Score'], errors='coerce')

# 'Spotify' integer nullable
df_merged['Spotify'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merged['Spotify'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Step 5: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'Artist',
    'Year Inducted',
    'Years Waited',
    '# of Years Nominated',
    'Influenced',
    'Certified Units (Millions)',
    'Albums in RS500',
    'Top 100 Singles',
    'Highest Position',
    'Times on Cover of RS',
    'Score',
    'Spotify'
]

df_final = df_merged[target_columns]

# Step 6: Export the final dataframe to CSV
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/training_7.csv", index_col=0)

# Join all tables on 'Artist' using source2 as the base (dimension table with most columns)
df = source2.merge(source7, on='Artist', how='inner') \
            .merge(source6, on='Artist', how='inner') \
            .merge(source0, on='Artist', how='inner') \
            .merge(source5, on='Artist', how='inner') \
            .merge(source3, on='Artist', how='inner') \
            .merge(source1, on='Artist', how='inner') \
            .merge(source4, on='Artist', how='inner')

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns of the target schema that are unique identifiers:
# 'Artist' (string), 'Year Inducted' (float but used as group by because it is a key attribute in target),
# 'Years Waited' (int), '# of Years Nominated' (int)
# Aggregations: max for all other columns to collapse duplicates and keep values consistent with target examples
grouped = df.groupby(['Artist', 'Year Inducted', 'Years Waited', '# of Years Nominated'], dropna=False).agg({
    'Influenced': 'max',
    'Certified Units (Millions)': 'max',
    'Albums in RS500': 'max',
    'Top 100 Singles': 'max',
    'Highest Position': 'max',
    'Times on Cover of RS': 'max',
    'Score': 'max',
    'Spotify': 'max'
}).reset_index()

# Write the final output
grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_71/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
